answer: A sybil attack floods the network with fake agents. Stop it with a velvet gate: each newcomer waits in a queue before a rotating signing server that checks a bloom filter for duplicates, then issues exactly one credential per verified IP path. This turns sybil flooding into a hardware coordination problem — not a free lunch. Honest agents arrive slowly, a rare sonnet of reliable computation rising above the noise, proof that when slots are scarce, an oasis of trust survives.
